vulnerabilities.title: STACK_BUFFER_OVERFLOW_IN_PRINT_BOARD_SPRINTF_ACCUMULATION

root_cause.description: In print_board, sprintf is called with the destination buffer (buf at rbp-0x1090) as both the output target AND the first %s format argument. This self-referential pattern (sprintf(buf, fmt, buf, ...)) causes each sprintf call to APPEND to the existing buffer content by reading it via %s and writing the result back to the same buffer. The buffer content area is 0x1000 (4096) bytes, but the accumulated content grows with each round displayed. With size=26, max_rounds=(26+1)*2=54, and each round adding ~84 bytes (data line + border line), the total content reaches 4662 bytes, overflowing the 4096-byte content area by 566 bytes. The overflow corrupts inline format strings stored at buf+0x1000/0x1020/0x1040, the pad buffer at buf+0x1060, the stack canary at rbp-0x8, saved rbp, and the return address. No bounds checking is performed on the accumulated content size, and the sprintf return value is never checked.

attack_surface.input: gameboard_size (1-26) via read_int in init; guess strings via read_all in play_round
data_flow: User inputs gameboard_size via read_int (stdin) in init
size stored to context+0x20 (context.size), checked 1 <= size <= 26
init_game sets max_rounds = (size+1)*2, stored to context+0x4
play() loop calls print_board() at start of each iteration
print_board() iterates i from 0 to round_idx-1, calling sprintf for each round
sprintf(buf, fmt, buf, ...) accumulates content: each call reads existing buf content via %s and appends new data
Content grows by ~84 bytes per round (42-byte data line + 42-byte border line)
When round_idx >= 48 (size=26), total content exceeds 4096-byte buffer area
Overflow corrupts format strings, pad buffer, canary, saved rbp, return address
printf('\n%s\n', buf) at end of print_board prints accumulated content to stdout

security_check.expected: Bounds check on accumulated content length before each sprintf call, or use of snprintf with buffer size limit, or tracking of total bytes written
security_check.actual: No bounds checking whatsoever. sprintf (not snprintf) is used with unbounded accumulation. The sprintf return value (number of bytes written) is never checked or used to limit subsequent writes.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing content length validation against buffer capacity (0x1000=4096 bytes). The self-referential sprintf(buf, fmt, buf, ...) pattern inherently causes unbounded growth with no termination condition based on buffer capacity.

vulnerable_operation.operation: sprintf with self-referential buffer as destination and %s argument
vulnerable_operation.address: 0x18cf (first border sprintf), 0x1929 (header sprintf), 0x1983 (second border sprintf), 0x1a51 (per-round data sprintf), 0x1aaf (per-round border sprintf)
vulnerable_operation.expression: sprintf(buf, fmt, buf, ...) where buf is at [rbp-0x1090] with 0x1000 byte content area
vulnerable_operation.target: Stack buffer [rbp-0x1090], overflow into [rbp-0x90] through [rbp+0x8] (format strings, pad, canary, saved rbp, return address)
vulnerable_operation.size: Up to 566 bytes overflow past 4096-byte content area (size=26, round_idx=54)

impact.reason: The stack buffer overflow writes up to 566 bytes past the 4096-byte content area, corrupting inline format strings, pad buffer, stack canary, saved rbp, and return address. The corruption occurs during sprintf execution before any canary check. The overflow content is partially attacker-controlled (guess strings embedded in round data lines).

Two crash paths: (1) Stack canary at [rbp-0x8] is corrupted when content reaches 4232 bytes (round_idx >= 49), triggering __stack_chk_fail at function return. (2) Corrupted format strings (overwritten when content exceeds 4096 bytes at round_idx >= 48) may cause sprintf to dereference invalid pointers or read invalid memory, causing SIGSEGV before the canary check.

When content overflows into format strings, the corrupted format strings are used by subsequent sprintf calls. If the corrupted format contains %s specifiers (potentially from attacker-controlled guess strings containing '%' characters), sprintf may read stack data from argument registers/stack positions. This data would be included in the buf content and printed to stdout by the final printf('\n%s\n', buf) call. This requires precise alignment of guess string '%' characters with format string offsets.

evidence.description: Stack allocation: 'sub rsp, 0x10a0' allocates 4256 bytes total. Buffer at [rbp-0x1090], canary at [rbp-0x8]. Content area is 0x1000=4096 bytes (from buf to format strings at buf+0x1000).

First sprintf call: sprintf(buf, format1, buf, pad_buf). rdi=buf (dest at rbp-0x1090), rsi=format1 (at buf+0x1000), rdx=buf (first %s source). buf is BOTH destination and first %s argument, causing content accumulation.

Per-round sprintf in loop: sprintf(buf, format3, buf, round_idx, guess_str, pad_buf, exact, partial). rdi=buf (dest), rdx=buf (first %s). Same self-referential pattern. format3='%s|%02i   |%s%s|R%02iW%02i|\n'. Each iteration adds ~42 bytes of data line content.
Per-round border sprintf: sprintf(buf, format1, buf, pad_buf). Same self-referential pattern. Each iteration adds ~42 bytes of border line content. Total per round: ~84 bytes.
Loop condition: 'cmp [rbp-0x1094], eax; jl 1997' where eax=context.round_idx. Loop iterates from 0 to round_idx-1. No check on accumulated content size.

Overflow calculation: with size=26, max_rounds=54, each round adds 84 bytes (42 data + 42 border). Header adds 126 bytes (3 lines * 42). Total at round_idx=54: 126 + 54*84 = 4662 bytes. Content area is 4096 bytes. Overflow = 566 bytes. Canary at offset 4232 corrupted at round_idx=49. Return address at offset 4248 corrupted at round_idx=50.
max_rounds = (size+1)*2. For size=26: max_rounds=54. For size=24: max_rounds=50 (overflow=24B). For size=25: max_rounds=52 (overflow=291B). Overflow occurs at size >= 24.
Final output: printf('\n%s\n', buf) prints accumulated buffer content to stdout. If corrupted sprintf read stack data into buf via unintended %s, that data would be leaked.

verification_required: Dynamic verification: run with size=26, play 49+ rounds without winning, confirm stack buffer overflow occurs
Dynamic verification: confirm __stack_chk_fail is triggered at print_board return
Dynamic verification: test if corrupted format strings cause sprintf crash before canary check
Dynamic verification: test if attacker-controlled '%' in guess strings can create format specifiers in corrupted format string area
Dynamic verification: confirm overflow amounts for size=24 and size=25

vulnerabilities.title: UNINITIALIZED_STACK_MEMORY_READ_IN_PRINT_BOARD_FIRST_SPRINTF

root_cause.description: In print_board, the content buffer at [rbp-0x1090] (4096 bytes) is not initialized before the first sprintf call. The first sprintf uses buf as the first %s argument (sprintf(buf, format1, buf, pad_buf)), which reads the uninitialized stack memory via %s until a NUL byte is found. On the very first call to print_board (when round_idx=0), there is no previous buf[0]=0x00 to terminate the %s read, so uninitialized stack data from prior function calls (init, generate_answer, etc.) may be read and incorporated into the output buffer. On subsequent calls, buf[0] is set to 0x00 at address 0x1ae8, so the %s reads 0 bytes and the issue does not recur.

affected_objects: Stack buffer at [rbp-0x1090] (uninitialized content area, 4096 bytes)

data_flow: init() and related functions use stack space for local variables
play() calls print_board() for the first time
print_board allocates 0x10a0 bytes on stack (sub rsp, 0x10a0)
Content area [rbp-0x1090] to [rbp-0x90] is NOT zeroed
First sprintf(buf, format1, buf, pad_buf) reads buf via %s
Uninitialized stack data is read until NUL byte found
Data is incorporated into output and printed by printf

security_check.expected: Buffer should be zeroed (memset/memset to 0) before first use, or buf[0] should be explicitly set to 0x00 before the first sprintf
security_check.actual: Buffer is not initialized. The code relies on buf[0]=0x00 from the previous print_board call (set at 0x1ae8), but this does not exist on the first call.

The leaked data could include residual stack content from init(), generate_answer(), generate_tokenset(), or init_game(). The exact content depends on prior stack usage. This only occurs on the first print_board call; subsequent calls have buf[0]=0x00.
